memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax she had laid out on the roof. So the men set out in pursuit of the spies on the road that leads to the fords of the Jordan, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut. — Josh 2:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rahab had hidden the spies under stalks of flax drying on her flat rooftop — an ordinary household detail that becomes the very cover God uses to protect His men. The pursuers rush off down the wrong road, and behind them the city gate slams shut, sealing them outside and the spies safely within.

There is something quietly reassuring here. God often works His protection through the plainest of means. Not a lightning bolt from heaven, not an angelic army — just some flax on a roof and a closing gate. We sometimes look for God only in the dramatic, and miss His hand in the ordinary provisions all around us.

Rahab used what she had. She did not have great resources or power; she had a rooftop, some flax, and a willing heart. God takes what is in our hands and makes it enough for His purposes. Small obedience placed in God's hands accomplishes great things.

The whole scene reminds us that God is never caught off guard. While the king's men chased shadows, God's plan moved forward without a stumble. The same God who guarded those spies watches over His people still, often through means so ordinary we almost fail to notice them (Rom 8:28).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might God be protecting or providing for you through "ordinary" means you overlook?
2. What small thing is in your hands right now that God could use?
3. Do you look for God only in the dramatic, or also in the everyday?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, open my eyes to see Your hand in ordinary things. Use what little I have for Your purposes, and help me trust that You are never caught off guard. Amen.
